snapshot.notes: Hand-curated registry of upcoming directly elected mayoral contests in England. Only contests with a statutory instrument, an official council announcement, or an established statutory cycle are listed as confirmed. Figures in prior_result blocks are verified against the returning authority before publication.
snapshot.voting_system_note: The English Devolution and Community Empowerment Act 2026 (Royal Assent 29 April 2026, section 63 and Schedule 30) restored the supplementary vote for mayoral and PCC elections. Commencement: SI 2026/656 brought the change into force on 18 June 2026 for elections whose notice is published on or after that date. The 7 May 2026 mayoral elections were the last under first past the post; every contest below uses the supplementary vote.

watchlist.label: Mayor of Lancashire
watchlist.status_note: No Lancashire mayoral election is scheduled and nothing is confirmed by order. The Lancashire Combined County Authority remains non mayoral. Reporting at the start of August 2026 puts a possible first election at 2028 at the earliest and stresses it is far from confirmed: the LCC opposition leader has asked for May 2027, the Blackburn and Blackpool leaders support a mayor, and the LCC and LCCA leader opposes. Government policy is not to impose mayors but to reach full strategic authority coverage of England by the end of 2028. The May 2027 Lancashire ballots are the shadow unitary elections only.

hypothetical_lancashire.label: Mayor of Lancashire (hypothetical)
hypothetical_lancashire.status_note: NO Lancashire mayoral election is scheduled and nothing is confirmed by order. This models what a county-wide supplementary vote mayoral contest WOULD look like on today's numbers, because the question keeps being asked. It is not a forecast of any scheduled election and will be replaced by a real forecast only if a contest is confirmed.
caveats: Hypothetical: no election exists, no date, no candidates, no confirmed mayoral geography. The Lancashire Combined County Authority is non mayoral.

The supplementary vote transfer calibration leans on the Greater Manchester by-election, a much more Labour leaning electorate than Lancashire. The transfer split is bloc symmetric (a Reform finalist gains eliminated Conservative second preferences at the same rate a Labour finalist gains Green and Liberal Democrat ones), but Restore Britain sits inside Other and is split 50/50, which likely understates Reform transfers in a Reform strong county. Treat Labour's runoff edge, where it appears, as an upper bound.
Turnout for a standalone mayoral contest would be low and uneven; neither base fully captures that.

sv_calibration.note: Supplementary vote transfer behaviour anchors, verified 8 August 2026 against the returning authorities. Derived parameters: transfer reach (share of eliminated candidates' votes that reach a finalist) was 60.8 percent in Greater Manchester 2026 (103,326 of 169,949; 66,623 exhausted) and 44.3 percent in London 2021 (276,863 of 624,585). Of transfers reaching the finalists in GM 2026, 56.2 percent went to the Labour finalist and 43.8 percent to the Reform UK finalist, despite the eliminated pool leaning right of centre (Restore Britain plus Conservative outweighed Green plus Liberal Democrats).

lancashire_pcc_2021.note: Con won 51.27-48.73. Eliminated pool LD 32,813 + Reform UK 17,926 (fringe-era Reform, 4.83pct: do NOT map onto 2026 Reform). Transfers derived from official first/final counts; OPCC publishes no exhausted breakdown.

lancashire_pcc_2016.note: Lab won. UKIP-era pool (UKIP 16.54pct + LD) split near-evenly Con/Lab: right-populist ballots did NOT break heavily Conservative in Lancashire.

gm_2026.district_signal: Official per-district table: Reform (Astley) WON second preferences in Wigan, Oldham, Rochdale, Tameside and Bury; Labour (Craig) dominated Manchester, Stockport, Trafford. Lancashire's geography resembles the former group, so pooled GM parameters lean Labour when applied to Lancashire.

may_2026_results_note: The six 7 May 2026 mayoral elections (Croydon, Hackney, Lewisham, Newham, Tower Hamlets, Watford) are in data/results/may-2026/local-and-mayor.merged.json and were the last first past the post mayoral contests. The devolution priority programme mayoral elections did not happen in May 2026: Cumbria and Cheshire and Warrington were deferred to May 2027 at the councils' request, and Greater Essex, Hampshire and the Solent, Norfolk and Suffolk, and Sussex and Brighton were delayed to May 2028 by the government on 4 December 2025.
